query: Which method can be used for the presence of ferromagnetic ground states, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The presence of chemical short-range order (SRO) in multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can increase the maximum strength and affect dislocation patterning, which may be related to the emergence of ferromagnetic ground states.
generation.conditions: Uniaxial tensile deformation at a constant engineering strain rate of 10^8 s^-1 and temperature of 300 K
generation.structural_mediator: Stacking fault energy (SFE) and antiphase boundary generation
generation.mechanism: The interplay between SRO, SFE, and antiphase boundary generation exerts back stress on moving dislocations, retarding their motion and enhancing solid solution strengthening
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased maximum strength and altered dislocation patterning
generation.boundary: The imposed straining rate in the simulations is several orders of magnitude higher than that of conventional laboratory experiments

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does chemical short-range order (SRO) affect the maximum strength and dislocation patterning in multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs)?. System: CrCoNi-based alloys. Processing: Hybrid Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. Test conditions: Uniaxial tensile deformation at a constant engineering strain rate of 10^8 s^-1 and temperature of 300 K. Findings: The presence of SRO appreciably increases the maximum strength and lowers the propensity for faulting and structure transformation; SRO increases the stacking fault energy (SFE) and activation energy barrier of dislocation motion; Grain orientation plays a crucial role in deformation mechanisms, microstructure evolution, and dislocation patterning; The volume fraction of deformation-induced hcp atoms is decreased in SRO systems compared to random solid solution (RSS) systems; SRO systems exhibit extended and strain-concentrated planar slip nanobands, implying repetitive dislocation glide. Mechanism: The interplay between SRO, SFE, and antiphase boundary generation exerts back stress on moving dislocations, retarding their motion and enhancing solid solution strengthening.
